pistons.headline: Pistons vs. Hornets final score: Cade Cunningham powers second-half surge in blowout win
pistons.body:
CHARLOTTE, NC - NOVEMBER 2: Cade Cunningham #2 of the Detroit Pistons looks on during the game against the Charlotte Hornets on November 2, 2026 at Spectrum Center in Charlotte, North Carolina. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and or using this photograph, User is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. Mandatory Copyright Notice: Copyright 2026 NBAE (Photo by Kent Smith/NBAE via Getty Images) | NBAE via Getty Images

The Detroit Pistons played great basketball throughout the night, but the Charlotte Hornets just kept hanging around. The Pistons were shooting better than 60% from the floor and 50% from three, and yet a Dennis Schroder layup made it a two-possession game with just under five minutes left in the second quarter. Then Cade Cunningham took over, then the Detroit Pistons took over, and suddenly a squeaker turned into a 124-91 Detroit win.

In that decisive 45-16 run, Cade Cunningham scored 14 points, and he did it in under three and a half minutes of game time. One of the league’s best players finally had his first superstar quarter of the season, scoring 17 points and notching three assists in total in that decisive third frame. He finished the night with 33 points, seven assists, and five steals. In those magical few minutes, he was everywhere in his bag. Patient mid-range pull-ups, slicing through the D for layups, catch-and-shoot threes. He went to the bench with 1:17 left in the third quarter, and you were left thinking he might hit 50 in the fourth. But he never needed to come back in the game again.

He saw the game was getting too close, and he decided to do something about it. He put the team on his back and said, “We’re playing too well to not blow these guys out.”

But the true blowout wouldn’t have happened without all the other contributions up and down the lineup. The Pistons really have something on offense this season, and while the range of ball handlers and actions can lead to some self-inflicted wounds, it is designed to open up this offense and let it breathe. And, boy, did they take a big gulping breath versus the Hornets.

The Pistons shot 57% from the floor and 48% from deep, and that was dragged down a bit as a consequence of some extended garbage time. The Pistons also kept their defense in top form. They forced 25 Charlotte turnovers, and that led to 27 fast-break points.

Detroit was led by Cade, but Duncan Robinson continues to be lights out this season. He shot 6-of-9 from deep on his way to 24 points. His stroke was immediate and effortless. He’s truly in the zone. Some of that shooting magic might be rubbing off on Kevin Huerter. The one-time bucket has struggled from deep for a few seasons now, including his short stint after a mid-season trade to Detroit last season. But he hit three threes tonight and is now shooting 38% from deep for the season. Even Ron Holland canned three threes tonight. Not to be overlooked is Ausar Thompson’s expanded role in the offense.

It’s not always perfect, but Thompson is getting more comfortable making decisions with the ball in his hands, and he’s understanding how to make defense pay by using his strength and burst to get something close to the basket. Thompson was 5-of-7 from the floor for 14 points, and he added six rebounds and four assists.

The Pistons had plenty of lopsided runs last season in their sprint to 60 wins. But those were driven by a defense that would suffocate you and an offense that could do just enough. Last year, the Pistons could go on a 27-2 run over the course of 17 minutes of game action. Tonight, they went on the same run in just over eight minutes.

Detroit’s defense remains the best in the league. Its offense is starting to catch up. That’s bad news for everyone else in the NBA.

It’s already time for a rematch, huh? The Detroit Pistons face the Charlotte Hornets for the second time this season. In the first matchup, the Pistons prevailed 97-89 behind a Cade Cunningham and Daniss Jenkins one-two punch at point guard. Cunningham had 30 points and seven assists, and Jenkins scored 14 points off the bench. They also got great contributions from Paul Reed (16 efficient points) and an all-around masterclass from Ausar Thompson, who tallied seven points, nine rebounds, and eight assists. It featured a great 31-point performance from the blossoming Brandon Miller and one of the season’s earliest head-scratchers. Naz Reid had seven points and six rebounds at halftime, but Hornets coach Charles Lee benched Reid for the entire second half for not meeting the “standards” of the team. Nothing stood out as egregious, and folks chalked it up to mixing up some defensive assignments and a lack of hustle. It was a surprising but short-lived kerfuffle (Reid’s been back in the lineup ever since). But I wouldn’t be surprised if the Hornets power forward is looking to make a statement against Detroit so as to truly put the situation to rest.

The Hornets are struggling to find their offense after moving on from LaMelo Ball and getting a bum hand via injuries — Kon Knueppel and Grant Williams are both going to miss the game tonight. That means the league’s least potent (statistically) offense is going to go up against the league’s most miserly defense (statistically). Detroit’s goal is to make that gulf clear and even wider at the end of the night than it was at the beginning.

pistons.headline: Pistons vs Nets final score: Detroit takes care of business in first NBA Cup game
pistons.body:
BROOKLYN, NY - OCTOBER 30: Ronald Holland II #5 of the Detroit Pistons dunks the ball during the game against the Brooklyn Nets during the 2026 Emirates NBA Cup on October 30, 2026 at Barclays Center in Brooklyn, New York. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and or using this Photograph, user is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. Mandatory Copyright Notice: Copyright 2026 NBAE (Photo by Nathaniel S. Butler/NBAE via Getty Images) | NBAE via Getty Images

The Detroit Pistons start the NBA Cup off with a bang. Detroit thumped the Brooklyn Nets 110-94. A plus-16 point differential is a solid start on their quest to win their first NBA Cup in franchise history.

Detroit’s defense got off to an uncharacteristic start. They got mixed up on several pick-and-roll possessions, but that didn’t last long. They figured out the Nets’ speedy guards. Nolan Traoré turns on the turbos when turning the corners. Detroit adjusted to his speed and Julius Randle’s bully ball style of play.

For the second straight game, Detroit held their opponents to a seemingly never-ending scoring drought. The Pistons hard-hedged, blitzed, and switched PnRs depending on their personnel on the floor. It’s a luxury to have so many versatile defenders.

The John Collins at the five lineups always present a different look. It’s a lot of speed out there when Detroit goes small. The lineups with Paul Reed aren’t technically small ball, but J.B. Bickerstaff can employ him so many different ways. Reed is not too much of a drop big, but he pressures guards coming off screens in every other way.

When Detroit did go small, Duncan Robinson and Kevin Huerter got their hands dirty helping the team gang rebound. It didn’t register in the box score every time, but the fight was there. Huerter was scrappy and hit a pair of first-half triples. His explosion from trey is coming. I will remain patient and will take all the other little things he’s doing.

Robinson is off to a career-best start. The 3s were hit or miss, but he thrived in transition and baited Brooklyn into several turnovers. Robinson is such an educated cutter. Teams press up on him, sticking to him like gum under the desk, but he has no issue using their momentum against them, beelining to the rim.

Robinson and Ausar connected on some backdoor cuts. Their synergy is so evident. They burned another defense with their DHO link-up.

We got aggressive Ausar tonight. Right from the opening tap, he searched for his shot and was content to put his head down to get to the rim.

Ausar Thompson that was beautiful pic.twitter.com/1Z3C6BE6Nd
— mm (@muhtxm) October 31, 2026

We got a middy pull-up in the second! Ausar was feeling it and took another jumper the following possession. Make or miss, that is the mentality that can change this team’s outlook.

Ausar’s all-around play was terrific. We’re watching a legit point forward in the making game by game. Ausar had six assists tonight. This one was gorgeous.

Ausar with the behind the back dish 👀 pic.twitter.com/rhArT0m6sk
— Detroit Pistons (@DetroitPistons) October 31, 2026

Ausar’s 9-to-5 defensive intensity clone, Ron Holland, had himself a ball game. He had a turnover and ill-advised fouls early on, but Holland turned it up a notch in the 3rd quarter.

The third-year wing was EVERYWHERE. His hound-em defense showed up, but Holland buried two 3-pointers during his energy blitz. He finished with 18 points, going 6-for-10 from the field, along with four steals.

It was another day in the office for Deuce. He might be the first player to get a foul called in their favor in real time. He did the classic Kobe/DWade up fake, then shoot while the defender is off their feet. It did not seem like the referee was going to reward Cade’s craftiness until he walked over there with wide-spread arms demanding an explanation. Nice to see Cade getting that superstar whistle these days. He dropped 20/5/4.

Brooklyn remains winless (0-5). Traoré is a blur, and Mikel Brown Jr. seems to process PnR coverages like a point guard who’s been around the block. That dude has promise. High process and deep-range shooting is always a dub in my book. Brooklyn fans won’t enjoy watching Randle go one-on-one with 10 eyes staring at him, waiting for his drive, but hey, it’s not all bad elsewhere. Focus on the young guards.

Ebuka Okorie probably gets more run in a typical blowout. Detroit aimed to run up the score for the cup point differential, so that might explain why Bickerstaff went with his proven horses until it was less than three minutes in the contest.

Detroit’s 2025 second-round pick Chaz Lanier got in on the action. He knocked down two deep balls with his quick trigger release. This was a monster performance from Detroit after their defense got back on a string. Brooklyn isn’t the 1996 Bulls but has competed in most of their games so far. Not tonight.

Detroit looks to beat up on the Charlotte Hornets again to kick off their November schedule on Monday. Maybe they get Charlotte so discombobulated that Charles Lee has to bench another starter.

(Daniss had another end-of-quarter buzzer-beater. Add this one to the highlight reel)

He's good at that. https://t.co/sYGm01ubBO pic.twitter.com/b6SJHj4SCu
— Detroit Pistons (@DetroitPistons) October 31, 2026

pistons.headline: Pistons vs. Nets preview:  NBA Cup Group Play begins
pistons.body:
There isn’t a whole lot you can complain about the Pistons start to the season.  They sit at an East-best 4-1 and got through the brutal start to their schedule with a 3-1 record.  This is all despite missing Jalen Duren for half of the games and key rotation players like Ausar Thompson and Isaiah Joe for a couple.

The Brooklyn Nets are 0-4, but they have been sneakily competitive this season with their only blowout loss being a 27-point loss to the Indiana Pacers.  They are coming off a buzzer beating loss to the Boston Celtics in overtime on Tuesday.

It is tough to make definitive judgments on a team early in the season, but I feel like Brooklyn could be one of those teams that doesn’t win a lot of games, but makes it tough on you every time you face them.

The Pistons have a good shot at winning their group in the NBA Cup, but I definitely wouldn’t call this game an “easy” win.

Game Vitals

Where:  Barclays Center in Brooklyn, NY
When:  Friday, October 30 at 7:30 pm EST
Watch:  TV20 Detroit or DAZN (streaming)
Odds:  Pistons (-7.5)

Analysis

An underrated factor to this game is that the Brooklyn Nets were able to fly home from Boston after their overtime heartbreaker on Tuesday and have been home since then while the Pistons had to fly from New York, back to Detroit for a home game against Charlotte, and then back to New York for this game.  They at least have a day of rest for this game, which should help, but having to travel that much in a 3-day span is not great.

This is very much could be a trap game given the travel-related factors and the fact that the Nets have been a pretty feisty team this season despite their 0-4 record.  The Nets have a pretty good mix of developing young players and veterans that make things easier for them, so I feel like they will be a tough out every night, even if their record is one of the worst in the league.

The two veterans that are the big threats are Julius Randle and Michael Porter Jr.  Both have kind of been sent to rot in Brooklyn by their former teams, but Porter put together an impressive season last year and continues to be one of the biggest off-ball shooting threats in the league.  Randle’s game is what it is at this point, but he has the ability to take on a pretty heavy offensive burden and allow the younger guys to focus on taking the easy shots.

One of the young players we will miss out on seeing is last year’s highest of their many first round picks, Egor Demin, who suffered a leg injury in the overtime loss to the Celtics.  The Nets still have other improving young players like 1st round pick Mikel Brown Jr. and Nolan Traore, who has shown some flashes in his 2nd season.

I have faith that the Pistons will be able to slow down the Brooklyn Nets on the defensive end, as they have only given up 98 points per game over the last three games.  But, in those three games they have only averaged 100 points per game.  Without their 2nd offensive threat in Jalen Duren as well as a drop off in shooting from Duncan Robinson and no Isaiah Joe, the free flowing offense that hit a lot of threes to start out the season is now temporarily missing in action (hopefully).

Luckily for the Pistons, there is a chance that Isaiah Joe returns tonight and their schedule over the next couple weeks while Jalen Duren is out is not as difficult as the gauntlet they started the season out with.

But, as long as the Pistons have Cade Cunningham, they have a chance in any game.  Cade finally broke out of his quiet start to the season to the tune of 30 points against Charlotte on Wednesday.  He hit multiple clutch shots along with Daniss Jenkins to seal the game.  With how much the Pistons have struggled to create offense without Jalen Duren, I expect the Jenkins-Cade backcourt to get a few more looks since both players can handle the ball and create a bit for others.

That’s not to say that we haven’t gotten that look before, as JB Bickerstaff has employed it a few times this season, but Jenkins is a player that had his best moments last season when he got a lot of minutes, so it is worth riding the hot hand.

If there is one factor that is in Brooklyn’s favor in this game, it is their frontcourt size.  Paul Reed has done a fantastic job filling in for Jalen Duren, but he is a bit undersized for a full-time starting center. Brooklyn has Day’Ron Sharpe, Julius Randle, and Michael Porter Jr. in their starting frontcourt and all three are 6’9” or above.  The only one of those three that can be classified as a “good” defender is Sharpe, but all of them are good rebounders so I could see the Nets having an advantage on the glass.

At full health, it is difficult to see a world where the Pistons lose this game, but without Jalen Duren to provide a bit more offensive punch and possibly not having Isaiah Joe, this could end up being another ugly game for the Pistons that they have to win with their defense.

Lineups

Brooklyn Nets (0-4):  Mikel Brown Jr, Nolan Traore, Michael Porter Jr, Julius Randle, Day’Ron Sharpe

Detroit Pistons (4-1):  Cade Cunningham, Duncan Robinson, Ausar Thompson, John Collins, Jalen Duren

Question of the Day

Do you think the Pistons continue to win ugly or do they finally break out of their offensive slump?

pistons.headline: Pistons vs Hornets final score: Detroit overcomes slow offensive start
pistons.body:
DETROIT, MI - OCTOBER 28: Cade Cunningham #2 and Daniss Jenkins #24 of the Detroit Pistons look on during the game against the Charlotte Hornets on October 28, 2026 at Little Caesars Arena in Detroit, Michigan. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and/or using this photograph, User is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. Mandatory Copyright Notice: Copyright 2026 NBAE (Photo by Brian Sevald/NBAE via Getty Images) | NBAE via Getty Images

The Pistons recovered after a slow first half to defeat the Charlotte Hornets 97-89. Detroit’s defense was Steady Eddy all night. Their offense came alive with 32 points in the third quarter.

Daniss Jenkins’ 3-point bomb to end the second quarter ignited their offensive run. He came through in crunch time with timely baskets and heads-up defense to offense possessions. Jenkins (14 pts, 60 FG%) keeps the confidence at all times.

Cade Cunningham led the way with 30 points, five boards, seven assists, and one turnover. He shot 4-9 from triple range. While Jalen Duren remains out with a hamstring injury, Paul Reed continues to be dependable. Reed was all over the floor, scoring 16 points and displaying his Barry Allen hands with three steals.

Duncan Robinson will be in the sniper of the year race. He buried three triples and was a +6 for the game. Robinson and Ausar’s dribble handoff game is chef’s kiss.

Teams sag so far off Ausar and are haunted-house scared of Robinson when he’s on the move. Ausar’s man has to come up and cover so much ground when they run a DHO, and Robinson is such a willing passer.

Those two connected on a killer Robinson-to-Ausar sequence leading to a big slam in the fourth. Ausar stuffed the stat sheet with seven points, nine boards, and eight assists. His last dime to Cade for a triple sealed the deal. We all want him to be more aggressive and take certain shots when he’s near the basket, but passes like that are why he plays his brand of basketball.

Brandon Miller attacked Robinson relentlessly on the other end. Whenever the Pistons gave up a switch, Miller looked to put his shoulder in 55’s chest to get a floater off. It’s really not fair to single out Robinson. It got to the point where Miller was getting boogie on whoever. 3s, push shots, tomahawk slams, Miller got off tonight.

Miller was a one-man army, dropping 31 points and snagging 12 boards. He and Dennis Schröder (14) were the Hornets’ only double-digit scorers. Moussa Diabaté, Grayson Allen, and Royce O’Neale chipped in with nine apiece.

Detroit doubled Charlotte with four double-digit scorers. The Hornets kept it close down the stretch, but Detroit pulled away with an uptick in defensive tenacity and big-time shot-making from their creators, Cade and Jenkins.

That was a gutsy win with the way Detroit came out flat offensively. Hopefully Detroit gets off to a better start Friday versus the Brooklyn Nets. That will be the Pistons’ first in-season tournament group stage game. Get busy and set the point differential right.

lions.headline: Detroit Lions create 2 roster spots, place Jimmy Rolder on IR
lions.body:
Detroit Lions linebacker Jimmy Rolder (41) celebrates a play against Minnesota Vikings during the second half at Ford Field in Detroit on Sunday, Nov. 1, 2026. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co

On Tuesday, the Detroit Lions announced two roster moves, both creating vacant spots on the team’s 53-man roster.

As expected, rookie linebacker Jimmy Rolder was placed on injured reserve after suffering what coach Dan Campbell called a season-ending injury. It was officially announced as a hamstring injury, and Campbell said surgery could be an option for the former Wolverine.

“Jimmy Rolder is going to require surgery, or he could. The point is this is a significant injury. He’ll be out for the season,” Campbell said on Monday.

It’s a tough break for Rolder. He missed much of training camp with a hamstring injury, and Sunday was his first significant action on defense all year. In just 17 snaps, Rolder recorded five tackles, a sack, and another tackle for loss. Combined with the indefinite loss of Jack Campbell, the Lions are a bit shorthanded at linebacker.

The other move the Lions made was waiving rookie safety Bishop Fitzgerald. Undrafted in 2026, Fitzgerald was signed off the Steelers’ practice squad when the Lions were particularly vulnerable at the safety position. But with Brian Branch returning recently—although in concussion protocol this week—and with Kerby Joseph returning soon, Fitzgerald may have just been the odd man out. It’s worth noting that last week, Campbell indicated that Thomas Harper was nearing a return from injury, as well.

With those two moves, the Lions now have two vacancies on the 53-man roster. One of those spots is expected to be taken by linebacker K.J Britt. On Monday, a report dropped that the Lions were signing the veteran special teamer off the Patriots’ practice squad, and Campbell confirmed it on his radio appearance on Tuesday.

At this point, it isn’t clear what the Lions plan to do with the other open roster spot.

lions.headline: NFL Week 9 power rankings: Lions’ rise continues but still have doubters
lions.body:
Nov 1, 2026; Detroit, Michigan, USA; Detroit Lions head coach Dan Campbell reacts in front of quarterback Jared Goff (16) during the first quarter against the Minnesota Vikings at Ford Field. Mandatory Credit: Lon Horwedel-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect

The Detroit Lions (5-2) have now won three in a row and beaten NFC North rivals—the Green Bay Packers in Week 7 and the Minnesota Vikings in Week 8—in back-to-back games.

The Lions’ balanced roster and adaptable coaching staff allow them to stay competitive with any opponent, and as we have seen in each of the three previous wins, they can beat an opponent in a variety of ways. Against the Cardinals, the Lions unleashed their passing attack; against the Packers, they controlled possessions and the clock; and last Sunday, they matched the Vikings’ aggression with an attacking run game and dominated on the ground. With each win, the Lions’ defense has steadily improved, though many national analysts are still looking at season-long stats instead of what they’ve done recently.

In this week’s power rankings, the Lions moved up in every ranking; however, they’re still one holdout away from being a consensus top-10 team. Let’s take a closer look at this week’s national power rankings.

Sports Illustrated: 4 (Previous rank: 7)

From Connor Orr:

Drew Petzing has been on my ascending head coaches list but has put himself on many others after a sterling performance against the Vikings. Petzing managed to get the job done against Brian Flores and add a flourish, a particular feat that seems almost impossible given how talented this Minnesota defense is.

NFL.com: 5 (Previous rank: 11)

From Nick Shook:

This might not age well, given the serious injury questions facing the Lions, but I’m giving them the boost because of how they finished their victory over the previously undefeated Vikings. Facing a 15-12 deficit in the fourth quarter, Detroit sliced right through Minnesota’s terrifying defense with apparent ease, leaning on Jahmyr Gibbs before finishing the drive with a beautiful touchdown pass from Jared Goff to Jameson Williams. The Lions won by sticking to their offensive identity, getting another encouraging showing from the defense and outlasting the Vikings in a victory that feels bigger than most.

The Athletic: 7 (Previous rank: 9)

From Chad Graff and Josh Kendall:

Reality check: The defense is still a problem

Detroit’s defensive EPA through eight weeks (minus-60.22) is the 16th-worst of any team in the last 10 years, according to TruMedia. Jahmyr Gibbs saved them Sunday by rushing for a career-best 99 yards after forcing a missed tackle, according to NextGenStats. He finished with 23 carries for 153 yards and now has more touchdowns in his first four seasons (59) than anyone other than Terrell Davis and LaDainian Tomlinson.

USA Today: 7 (Previous rank: 11)

From Nate Davis:

Does there need to be concern about RB Jahmyr Gibbs’ usage at some point? He’s on pace for 464 touches, which would be the second-highest total in NFL history. (James Wilder had 492 in 1984.)

Yahoo Sports: 8 (Previous rank: 10)

From Frank Schwab:

Biggest need: Defense, particularly at cornerback

The Lions’ fan base wasn’t happy when the Cowboys overpaid to get cornerback Joey Porter Jr. in a trade. They know that cornerback is an issue and it seems hard to believe the deadline will pass without Detroit doing something at the position.

Yet, there are other issues on a defense that has struggled most of the season, though it has allowed just 32 points the last two games. While the human element of linebacker Jack Campbell’s neck injury is overwhelming, and his recovery is the biggest part of that story, there is a football side to it as well. Detroit will presumably be without one of the best off-ball linebackers in the NFL indefinitely. While the team’s thoughts are primarily on their young star’s health, the Lions also have to deal with the reality of perhaps adding a linebacker before the deadline.

CBS Sports: 9 (Previous rank: 10)

From Pete Prisco:

They beat the Packers and the Vikings in consecutive weeks in low-scoring games. That’s a new formula for this team to win games, but a good sign.

ESPN: 9 (Previous rank: 11)

From ESPN Staff, excerpt from Eric Woodyard:

Best in-season trade acquisition ever: DE Za’Darius Smith in 2024

The Lions have plenty of impactful offseason trades, including ones that helped them land quarterbacks in Jared Goff (2021) and Bobby Layne (1950). But the best in-season deal in terms of immediate impact likely goes to Smith. He had four sacks in eight regular-season games for the Lions, who had a team-record 15 wins and earned the NFC’s No. 1 seed in 2024. Detroit received Smith and a 2026 seventh-round draft selection from the Browns for a 2025 fifth-rounder and a 2026 sixth-rounder.

Sporting News: 11 (Previous rank: 12)

From Vinnie Iyer:

The Lions have come through with huge back-to-back home division wins against the Packers and Vikings. The big surprise is the improved defense. After allowing an average of almost 30 points in the first five games, the Lions have given up only 32 total the past two weeks. They should keep up that play with the Dolphins in Miami next.

lions.headline: Film study: Cade Mays is still the Detroit Lions’ best center
lions.body:
Detroit Lions center Cade Mays (64) warms up ahead of the game between Detroit Lions and Minnesota Vikings at Ford Field in Detroit on Sunday, Nov. 1, 2026. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co

The Detroit Lions are 2-0 in the division and on a three-game win streak after ending the Minnesota Vikings’ undefeated start to the 2026 season. While the score only resulted in a 19-15 final, the Lions racked up 230 yards rushing against the NFL’s premier defensive unit.

Starting center Cade Mays entered the game in his second start of the season after suffering a fractured wrist in training camp. In his absence, backup Juice Scruggs had performed very well. Against Minnesota, Mays’ day was cut short after the first offensive possession in the second quarter, resulting in only 22 snaps played. Again, Scruggs filled in and played at a high level.

With Mays in the game, the Lions only rushed for 31 yards. With Scruggs, the team captured the remaining 199 yards on the ground in just under three quarters of play.

But correlation is not causation.

For this film study, I went back to watch the all-22 film of all 22 of Mays’ snaps against the Vikings. The quick conclusion is this: Mays did not lose a single rep of his one-on-one matchups in either the run or pass game. Despite the various looks, pre-snap shifts, and varied simulated blitzes, Mays’ day was about as flawless as you could ask for.

Below, I’ve clipped three plays that highlight the high-level play from Mays and capture the upside of what this offense can look like with him moving forward.

Athleticism and strength in the run game

The first play is an outside zone run play to the left. In the scheme, Mays is responsible for the gap to his left, but pre-snap there is no defender in the A-gap or even over the guard. The nearest defender is lined up in the B-gap as a 3-technique just outside of left guard Christian Mahogany. At the snap, the 3-technique defensive tackle stunts inside across Mahogany’s face and into Mays’ zone. Mays reaches the stunting defender, captures outside leverage by not stopping his feet at the point of contact, and continues to drive and strain through the whistle. The result: displacing the line of scrimmage for the soon-to-be MVP Jahmyr Gibbs to pick up a positive gain.

Anchor and strain in pass protection

The next play shown below highlights the size, strength, and finish Mays provides in the interior of the pocket for quarterback Jared Goff to rely on. At the snap, Mays absorbs and anchors against a strong bull rush from the defensive tackle, but once Goff steps up and the defender starts to swim out of his initial rush, Mays switches gears like a Ford F-150, driving his guy into the dirt once he gains leverage. If Goff had taken an extra moment to settle into the throw, the play could have resulted in Gibbs walking in for a touchdown.

Mental processing and physical adaptation

The final play highlighted below shows how Mays was able to mentally process the simulated pressure of the linebacker lined up as the 0-technique right over him and adjust when the blitz did not materialize. Not only does Mays make the initial recognition, but he is also able to adapt to pick up the presnap B-gap blitzing linebacker who stunts into the A-gap. From there, Mays picks up the defender and establishes leverage by moving his feet and hips to prevent the pocket from collapsing. The result is enough time for Goff to deliver the biggest explosive pass of the game, a 46-yard deep shot to Jameson Williams in stride.

The aim of this film study was not to put down or dismiss Scruggs’ performance, which was very strong in its own right. In fact, Dan Campbell was asked on 97.1 about Scruggs and whether his quality play has started a competition at the center position.

“… to get thrust back in there against that defense with everything that they were doing, to have that production, I mean, that was impressive. He was locked in. He was so ready to go. He was. I told you this before, we love Juice. He just fits us. He’s all about business, he’s a great teammate, he’s high-energy, he tries to finish plays, runs off the football. So he did a heck of a job.

As of right now, he’s our guy, because I don’t see Cade practicing Wednesday and he might not Thursday. So we’re going to get Juice ready to go here.”

At the end of the day, the Lions have two starting-caliber NFL centers on their roster. This is a huge credit to Brad Holmes for his effort in transforming the offensive line this offseason. The takeaway is clear, though. The ceiling for the Lions’ offense is highest with Cade Mays as the point man.

lions.headline: Detroit Lions injury updates: More on Kerby Joseph, Cade Mays, D.J. Reed
lions.body:
Detroit Lions quarterback Jared Goff (16) and center Cade Mays (64) warm up ahead of the game between Detroit Lions and Minnesota Vikings at Ford Field in Detroit on Sunday, Nov. 1, 2026. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co

On Tuesday morning, Detroit Lions coach Dan Campbell made his weekly radio appearance on 97.1 The Ticket’s “Costa & Jansen with Heather” show. During the interview, Campbell provided several personnel updates, given the mounting injuries.

He didn’t offer much of an update on Lions linebacker Jack Campbell, other than to say that he is “improving.”

Here are some other updates Campbell offered.

Kerby Joseph won’t play vs. Dolphins

Lions safety Kerby Joseph will be entering his second week of practice after the Lions started his evaluation clock last week. This week, it sounds like Joseph will get more involved in team reps, but Campbell has already ruled him out from playing this Sunday against the Miami Dolphins.

“We’re going to try and give him some scout team reps. He’s not going to play this game,” Campbell said. “I know that (question) was coming. He’s not playing vs. Miami. He’s just going to get some reps in practice.”

Joseph continues to ramp up from a knee injury that has sidelined him for over a year. At this point, it’s unclear when the team will attempt his return to game action.

Lions preparing Juice Scruggs to start vs. Miami, but no center competition… yet

Lions starting center Cade Mays is reportedly dealing with a low-ankle sprain, and it sounds like Detroit is not expecting him to play against the Dolphins this week. Campbell indicated that they are preparing backup Juice Scruggs to play.

“As of right now, he’s our guy, because I don’t see Cade practicing Wednesday and he might not Thursday,” Campbell said. “So we’re going to get Juice ready to go here.”

And while the offense turned a corner seemingly the moment Scruggs replaced Mays on Sunday against the Vikings, Campbell rebuffed a question suggesting there is a starting center competition between Mays and Scruggs when both are healthy.

“Well, I can’t say that right now,” Campbell said.

That said, he did talk about how impressed he was by Scruggs’ ability to turn what was mostly a week of mental reps at center into the performance he had against a tough Vikings defense.

“What I would say is that Juice came in and played very well,” Campbell said. “That’s what I would definitely say. He took the mental reps this week, he got a couple live, but really it was more mental at center, and to get thrust back in there against that defense with everything that they were doing, to have that production, I mean, that was impressive. He was locked in. He was so ready to go.”

Still waiting on D.J. Reed, others

Campbell didn’t provide any real substantive updates on Reed (hip), D.J. Wonnum (concussion), Brian Branch (concussion), or Jacob Saylors (neck). He did note that he doesn’t believe Reed or Saylors will practice on Wednesday, and they won’t know more about Branch or Wonnum’s progress through the concussion protocol until later on Tuesday.

Here’s exactly what he said about Reed specifically:

“Reed’s got a hip. There again, it doesn’t look good for him on Wednesday for sure. So until I can get more on that, I don’t see where he’s at,” Campbell said.

With how well Reed has been playing as of late, his loss—even for one week—could be costly, as Detroit continues to navigate a lot of turbulence in the secondary.

lions.headline: Detroit Lions stock report: 15 risers, 10 fallers against the Vikings
lions.body:
DETROIT, MICHIGAN - NOVEMBER 1: Sione Vaki #33 of the Detroit Lions runs with the ball during the first quarter against the Minnesota Vikings at Ford Field on November 1, 2026 in Detroit, Michigan. (Photo by Todd Rosenberg/Getty Images) | Getty Images

A tidal wave of frightened, silent uncertainty swept across Ford Field as the stadium realized Jack Campbell was also still down, motionless, after initially seeing Jimmy Rolder injured on the same play early in the fourth quarter. It felt strange that after such a drawn-out, worrisome delay in the game, both teams had to immediately bounce back for a crucial Vikings fourth-down attempt near the red zone in the middle of a divisional dogfight.

It felt strange, but it also felt powerful. This was a tougher recap article to gather my thoughts on, but the prevailing feeling after Jack Campbell was injured and taken to the hospital was a reminder of how powerfully unifying sports can be, even as a distraction from something far more important. Because the Detroit Lions fought with a sense of added vigor, pride, and togetherness in the fourth quarter. They battled for their brother, with everyone seemingly executing more sharply and in seamless synchronization. All of the Lions were competing for Jack. And it paid off, as they started 2-0 in the NFC North with an uncharacteristic 19-15 victory over the Vikings.

The Lions were physical and resilient. They were grit personified again, finishing the football game strong, exactly in the image of their head coach, Dan Campbell, and the values they pride themselves on. The same values that helped them rise from the ashes of the Matt Patricia-Bob Quinn era. Jack Campbell will hopefully have been proud of his team’s efforts.

For the second week in a row, they found a way to win ugly in the muddy abyss. Let’s embrace that resilient effort while taking a look at the Week 8 Stock Report, as the team improved to 5-2, while sending all our positive thoughts and support to Jack Campbell, his family, and the hospital staff caring for him.

Stock up: Jahmyr Gibbs & Sione Vaki, RB

Against one of the best defenses in football, the Detroit Lions might have found their new one-two punch at running back, and they proved it when it mattered most, when their team needed it most, as they wore down the Vikings’ defense in Vaki’s breakout performance.

The duo combined for a modest 16 carries for 66 rushing yards (4.1 yards per carry) in the first half. While Gibbs was swimming upstream battling outside-zone run calls, Vaki started running through the Vikings’ defense like a stick of dynamite blowing through a mountain, opening holes big enough for a locomotive. The Lions soon realized they could start beating Brian Flores’ defense by getting Gibbs involved in gap-scheme runs, too.

In the second half, Sonic & Tails erupted, bruising their way to a combined 18 carries for 152 rushing yards (8.4 yards per carry), including 143 yards after contact, 12 missed tackles forced, and six runs of 10-plus yards, with only one run stuff!

They set the tone and served as the catalysts for the team’s re-established identity, running through the Vikings’ defense for 230 rushing rushing yards and 5.9 yards per carry, a combination that no offense had accomplished against Minnesota in the Brian Flores era.

Stock up: D.J. Reed, CB

After the Detroit Lions’ defense crumbled against the Carolina Panthers, one of the potential avenues for improvement was D.J. Reed elevating his level of play after slumping through the first month of the season, getting exposed on deep balls and by bigger, contested-catch wide receivers.

Reed has responded emphatically and is playing some of the best football of his career. Starting with the turnover department, following the two-minute warning, Reed got the Lions the ball back with a spectacular diving interception near midfield. The play led to a much-needed field goal before halftime.

Reed was once again lockdown in coverage, frequently matching up with Jordan Addison. Across 12 coverage snaps against Addison, Reed allowed three targets, no catches, and recorded the interception. Additionally, Reed smothered both Jauan Jennings and Justin Jefferson, allowing no targets across five coverage snaps against Jennings and four against Jefferson.

Reed’s level of play has lived up to the billing of his free-agent contract, and he should be a defensive pillar the Lions can continue to rely on as they tweak and strengthen the unit throughout the season and gear up for the postseason.

Stock down: Chuck Clark & Christian Izien, S

Continuing with the potential avenues for improvement coming out of that Panthers mauling, another area of hope for the Lions’ defense was improved safety play, particularly with the return of Brian Branch and potential return of Kerby Joseph.

Unfortunately, Branch left the game in the second quarter with a somewhat self-inflicted and unfortunate concussion after playing just 23 defensive snaps. This resulted in Chuck Clark playing all 53 defensive snaps, while Christian Izien also emerged from the doghouse for eight defensive snaps, having already seen the field prior to Branch’s injury.

Neither Clark nor Izien is particularly comfortable dropping backward to take away areas of the field, holding up in man coverage, or operating in space. Both are ideally relegated to a specific Oscar the Grouch role, most comfortable in the congested confines of a trash can, where they can come downhill with physicality as a third box defender.

Clark missed a tackle attempt on a Jordan Mason run up the middle for a first down, hesitantly coming downhill with little confidence from a single-high safety look. Meanwhile, Izien was beaten in one-on-one coverage in the red zone on T.J. Hockenson’s fourth-quarter touchdown.

The Lions’ pass rush wasn’t quite there against Minnesota, averaging 3.26 seconds to pressure, by far their slowest mark of the season. A more capable quarterback-playcaller combination than Kyler Murray and Kevin O’Connell might have put Clark under the microscope after Branch’s injury, attacking him and exploiting his lack of mobility in coverage space. You still can’t rule out adding another safety at the trade deadline, but Thomas Harper can’t get healthy quickly enough.

Quick Hits

STOCK UP

Jameson Williams, WR: Williams, first and foremost, was blocking like a man possessed, helping generate extra yards for his running backs and Amon-Ra St. Brown. He more than made up for his taunting penalty with a game-high 70 receiving yards on four receptions and a touchdown. His 46-yard deep ball set up Detroit’s first field goal, his second reception put them in range for their second successful three-pointer before halftime, and he scored the game-winning touchdown.

Penei Sewell & Christian Mahogany, LT & LG: Sewell had a very uncharacteristic day with penalties, not all of which were justified, and Mahogany did get beaten quickly by Jalen Redmond for a pressure, but the left side of the offensive line was mowing people down in the run game. Drew Petzing and the running backs could rely on those two like the box office of a Pirates of the Caribbean movie, with the way they were opening holes like cannonballs. Sewell also shut out Dallas Turner across 12 pass-protection snaps.

Cade Mays & Juice Scruggs, C: While the Lions’ offense improved when Scruggs entered the game, that had more to do with Petzing’s adjustments than anything else. Both played well, with Mays opening a handful of holes on the few successful first-half runs and Scruggs being a rock in pass protection while handling the nose tackle backside on several successful second-half runs. The Lions are in the enviable position of having two above-average starting-caliber centers.

Alim McNeill, DT: While it wasn’t his most effective game as a pass rusher, he still provided excellent second effort to corral Murray for a sack on the junk play-action play. I also felt he was particularly forceful at the point of attack as a run defender.

Skyler Gill-Howard, DT: After disappearing against the Packers, which happens with developing rookies over a long season, Gill-Howard worked veteran RG Will Fries for a sack of Murray. But his most impressive play was a wildly athletic run stop on Aaron Jones, where he took on a double-team and balanced his way through it like a cat always landing on its feet. The defense will need everyone to step up amid the injuries, particularly to their Captain Jack, and Gill-Howard is someone who can still tap into his untapped potential.

Malcolm Rodriguez, LB: After not getting any run against the Packers, Rodriguez clearly showed the coaches something in practice to earn playing time immediately on the first defensive series. Rodriguez was also a brick thrown at Jordan Mason and the Vikings’ inept running game, recording two run stuffs against him, including one where he met the fullback in the hole. He now has an opportunity to step up into a more every-down role with injuries to Campbell and Jimmy Rolder.

Derrick Barnes, LB: Not a particularly strong day overall, although his fourth-quarter run stuff of Jordan Mason near the goal line was great. The Lions will need Barnes to figure things out and play his best football moving forward with Campbell absent, especially with the possibility of Barnes taking over the green dot.

Keith Abney II, S: Played only 28 defensive snaps and wasn’t targeted in coverage. It’s time for the Lions to take off the training wheels and let him rip one into a mailbox and bounce back (a bike analogy for a former figure-skating prodigy, Al?). The Dolphins’ inept passing attack, injured Patriots offense, and Buccaneers offense reminiscent of the 1946 national champion Army Black Knights with Heisman Trophy winner Glenn Davis provide the runway he needs to grow and prove himself at his new position.

Jack Fox, P: One of his best games of the season, booming a 46.5-yard net punting average (second-best of the season), with three punts downed inside the 20 (tied for his season high), including two at the 10-yard line, and only one return for no yards. As the offense struggled to figure out the Vikings’ defense in the first half, Fox gave Detroit’s defense some breathing room by pinning Minnesota deep.

Drew Petzing, OC: After a first half in which the passing attack was pretty much neutralized outside of Williams’ deep ball, Petzing made adjustments and won a second-half chess match with defensive mad scientist Brian Flores. Was a real in-game problem-solver.

STOCK DOWN:

Amon-Ra St. Brown, WR: A surprising performance, even with the amount of seven-man protections, as he wasn’t able to find more opportunities to get open and provide a security outlet for Jared Goff against the blitz.

Aidan Hutchinson, DE: He brought effort as a run defender, but this was his first game in some time as a non-factor rushing the passer, partly due to some of the Vikings’ play-action throwing platforms and being swallowed up by Vikings RT Brian O’Neill.

Eric O’Neill, DE: Needs to find a way to make an impact during his rare snap opportunities, especially when he can pin his ears back in obvious passing situations. With DJ Wonnum suffering an injury, Ahmed Hassanein may be active and have an opportunity to prove himself as a pass rusher. It’s a different role than O’Neill’s, but they’re still competing for some of the same snaps.

Roger McCreary, Rock Ya-Sin & Khalil Dorsey, CB: The cornerback rotation wasn’t nearly as big of a hit as it was against the Packers, with McCreary missing tackles in run defense, Ya-Sin losing matchups with T.J. Hockenson, and Dorsey getting beaten deep by Jordan Addison.

Ennis Rakestraw Jr., CB: Perhaps still dealing with the ankle injury he suffered against the Packers, but playing just one defensive snap was unexpected.

Brian Branch, S: Felt a little like Alim McNeill’s deflating second game back from injury against the Vikings last year. Branch needs to find a way to stay on the field.

STOCK NEUTRAL

Jared Goff, QB: Let’s be clear, Jared Goff the blocker is stock up. But he was a little stuck in the mud holding onto the football in the first half, taking four sacks and throwing an unfortunate interception, before responding well with great command of the offense against the blitz in the second half, even if the box score isn’t something to brag to your buddies about.

Sam LaPorta, Brock Wright & Tyler Conklin, TE: A weird day for the tight ends, as they made a few plays as receivers, fewer than expected for LaPorta, and all struggled in pass protection, which can be a tough ask. However, they were essential to the success of the running game.

DETROIT, MI - DECEMBER 05: Jack Campbell #46 of the Detroit Lions looks on from the sideline prior to an NFL football game against the Green Bay Packers at Ford Field on December 5, 2024 in Detroit, Michigan. (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images

It didn’t feel like a Victory Monday, and it sure as hell didn’t feel like a divisional Victory Monday this week.

There’s a dark cloud hovering over Allen Park these days, and as we continue to await actual, tangible good news on the health of Detroit Lions linebacker Jack Campbell, I’ve officially moved into the anger stage of grief.

Lions vs. Vikings Song of the Game: Soldier’s Poem by Muse

Jack Campbell has given everything to this team. He’s committed nearly his entire life to football.

And, yes, that has resulted in wonderful, amazing opportunities only a few of us could dream of. He got a college education and was drafted in the first round of the 2023 NFL Draft. In May, he signed a contract worth more money than most of us will see in 10 lifetimes.

But on Sunday, we got a terrible reminder that football can take nearly all of that back in an innocent-looking instant.

No amount of money or fame can prepare you for that kind of physical and emotional trauma. We justify the violence and terrible, long-term impacts this game has on its players because we give them fame and fortune. Then we convince ourselves that they know the implicit danger they are heading into, and it’s not our fault they made that decision.

But do they really know the risk? Is an NFL prospect who’s not even old enough to buy beer really capable of understanding just how life-altering even a short career in football can be? At that age, you feel invincible. And showing any sort of vulnerability or doubt will cost you your roster spot. Do you think most college players even saw the study a couple of months ago that found that among 235 former NFL players who donated their brains posthumously from 2016 to 2021, 91.5% of them had chronic traumatic encephalopathy (CTE)?

As someone who has not only paid thousands of dollars to watch this bloodsport, but now actively profits off of it—while putting zero of my life at risk—it forces me to rethink a lot of things. Jarring reminders like Sunday provide a glimpse into how ugly this whole operation is, and it’s hard not to feel complicit.

When you know damn well that this is wrong?
I would still lay down my life for you

And yet, despite all of that, I’m confident that a fully informed Jack Campbell would change very little in his life up until this point. The man loves football, and more importantly, he loves the process. He loves putting in a full day of work and throwing everything into the task in front of him.

One of Campbell’s most remarkable quotes came in his press conference after signing an $81 million deal. In a moment in which he became one of the highest-paid linebackers in NFL history, he, instead, admired the work, not the profits.

“I’ve just got a deep appreciation for people who show up to work every single day, even if no one notices, even if no one writes stories about them,” Campbell. “(They) get to work, do their job, and take care of their families and keep their families first. Just a great appreciation. It’s literally what the city of Detroit epitomizes, so that’s what I’m going to try to epitomize.”

Campbell followed through on that promise. He sacrificed so much of his time, effort, and now his body to this game that he loves, and there’s something tragically beautiful about that.

But in this moment, nothing feels beautiful about it. His sacrifices feel fruitless.

In an outstanding story for The Athletic, Campbell talked about his ultimate goal to give back to the people who awarded him financial stability for the rest of his life.

“How can I bring a Super Bowl to Detroit? How can I do everything in my power, with every waking second inside and outside of the building, to do that?”

Now, despite putting more into that goal than arguably any other player on the team, he may never get that opportunity. His days of putting in that work he so admires may be over forever in Allen Park.

It may be callous to compare Campbell’s plight to that of a soldier. He gets paid millions for our entertainment, while a soldier barely gets paid enough to eat in exchange (in theory) for our safety. But it sucks all the same that the people who give up so much of their own life for us rarely seem to get the kind of recompense they deserve.

There’s no justice in this world,
and there never was.

If you want to relive previous Lions seasons, you can find the playlists we curated below: 2016, 2017, 2018, 2019, 2020, 2021, 2022. And if you want to read previous versions of our Song of the Game columns, you can find those here.

lions.headline: Discussion: Which NFC contenders will miss the playoffs?
lions.body:
SEATTLE, WASHINGTON - NOVEMBER 02: Montez Sweat #98 of the Chicago Bears tackles Sam Darnold #14 of the Seattle Seahawks during the third quarter of the game at Lumen Field on November 02, 2026 in Seattle, Washington. (Photo by Steph Chambers/Getty Images) | Getty Images

With the Chicago Bears’ emphatic win over the Seattle Seahawks on Monday night, the NFC playoff picture is starting to become more clear, and it sure involves a lot of NFC North teams. After eight weeks, here’s the full playoff picture in the NFC.

Division leaders:

49ers: 6-1

Vikings: 6-1

Giants: 4-2-1

Panthers: 3-4

Wild Card race (top three advance)

5. Bears: 6-2
6. Lions: 5-2
7. Packers: 5-3

8. Seahawks: 4-4
9. Rams: 4-4
10. Buccaneers: 3-5
11. Falcons: 3-5
12. Cardinals: 3-5
13. Cowboys: 3-5
14. Commanders: 2-4-1
15. Saints: 2-5
16. Eagles: 2-6

The way I currently see it, the only teams truly in contention are the top nine teams listed in the standings. Granted, the Bucs and Falcons could very well jump the Panthers in the NFC South, but it feels like a pretty safe bet at this point that only one of those three teams will make the postseason. Combine that with a Giants team comfortably in the lead in the NFC East, and there are really only five other playoff spots that seem up for grabs and seven teams vying for those five spots:

49ers

Vikings

Bears

Lions

Packers

Seahawks

Rams

All seven of those teams have seen varying levels of success, and each team has some very strong strengths, and some weak weaknesses.

So today’s Question of Day is:

Which two teams amongst those seven contenders will miss the playoffs?

My answer: First, I just want to point to how difficult this question is. I think all seven of these teams are likely worthy of the postseason, and it’s unfortunate we have to let an NFC South team take at least one of their places.

Let me go backwards and announce the teams I’m most comfortable in making the playoffs. I think the Bears and 49ers both have a strong case for best team in the conference, as they are the only teams in the NFC that have both a top-10 scoring offense and defense.

Interestingly, the Rams are the next closest team with the 10th and 12th ranked offense/defense, so I’m going to have them IN, as well, despite their slow start. They’ve got a couple of cupcake games (Commanders, Cardinals) before their bye, and they should be much healthier by then. It’s admittedly a gauntlet of games after that (Packers, Chiefs, 49ers, Seahawks x2), but I’ve got them in.

I’m not 100% confident in the Lions, but I’m going to have them in, too. Their offense is humming with back-to-back strong performances against two of the best defenses in football (despite the low scoring). However, I am still significantly worried about their defense, particularly with the recent injuries. The defense played well over the last three games, but those were three poor offenses (Cardinals, Packers, Vikings).

That leaves the Vikings, Packers, and Seahawks fighting for the final spot. Before I dive into them, it’s worth considering strength of remaining schedule. The Vikings have by far the hardest road of these three teams.

Remaining strength of schedule, by opponent’s win percentage:

Vikings: .580

Packers: .561

Seahawks: .486

However, Minnesota has a two game lead over Green Bay and three over Seattle.

Could the Vikings truly fall out of playoff contention after a 6-0 start? The next three games (vs. Bills, at Packers, at 49ers) will tell us a lot. But they also have games against the Falcons, Panthers, Commanders, and Jets remaining. I think they likely get to 10-11 wins, which will probably be enough to make it.

The Packers and their struggling run game will also be tested soon. Their next three games are Patriots, Vikings, and Rams—with the Bills, Bears, and Lions still on the docket. They lose all of those games, and they’re already at nine losses.

And while the Seahawks have the easiest schedule, with games against the Raiders, Cardinals, Cowboys, Eagles, and Panthers remaining, I can see them dropping games to the 49ers, Giants, and Rams (x2) still. That offense is looking putrid right now, and I’m not sure how much their admittedly elite defense can help.

So my two teams out are the Packers and Seahawks. However, I think every NFC team outside the Bears and 49ers are capable of falling out of the race.

lions.headline: Detroit Lions signing veteran LB off Patriots practice squad
lions.body:
FOXBOROUGH, MASSACHUSETTS - OCTOBER 11: K.J. Britt #35 of the New England Patriots reacts during the fourth quarter against the Las Vegas Raiders at Gillette Stadium on October 11, 2026 in Foxborough, Massachusetts. (Photo by Kathryn Riley/Getty Images) | Getty Images

According to a report from ESPN’s Adam Schefter, the Detroit Lions are signing veteran linebacker K.J. Britt off of the New England Patriots’ practice squad.

The move comes after Detroit suffered two linebacker injuries on Sunday against the Minnesota Vikings. Rookie Jimmy Rolder suffered a season-ending hamstring injury, while Jack Campbell remains in the hospital with a neck injury. No specifics are known at this point about Campbell’s situation, but the team did say that early developments were “positive.”

Britt was a fifth-round draft pick for the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in 2021, and ended up playing 59 games for them over four seasons—including 15 starts. Last year, he was with the Miami Dolphins, playing in all 17 games and starting one. This year, he failed to make the Patriots’ 53-man roster, but they kept him around on the practice squad, and he was elevated for the team’s Week 5 game against the Raiders.

For most of his career, Britt has served as a special teamer. Across just over five seasons in the NFL, Britt has played 1,303 special teams snaps vs. 994 on defense—and he has logged over 250 special teams snaps in four of his first five NFL seasons.

There’s a good chance that will be Britt’s role early in Detroit. With the Lions likely to lean more heavily on the likes of Malcolm Rodriguez, Derrick Barnes, and Trevor Nowaske on defense—with potentially Amen Ogbongbemiga and Joe Bachie mixed in—the Lions will need more experienced depth on special teams and reserves on defense.

Britt should be a relatively good fit in Detroit, as a high-effort player who was a captain at Auburn.

#GoBucs coach Bruce Arians said that 5th-round pick K.J. Britt "looks like a football player, he walks like one, he talks like one. He’s a captain."

The former #Auburn LB @K_Britt10 describes his leadership style: pic.twitter.com/9frvWPxlLW
— Kyle Burger (@kyle_burger) May 16, 2021

Detroit should have a good handle on who Britt is as a person and player, as he overlapped with current Lions defensive line coach Kacy Rodgers during his entire time with the Buccaneers.

lions.headline: Detroit Lions Week 8 snap counts: How the defense adjusted to multiple injuries
lions.body:
DETROIT, MICHIGAN - NOVEMBER 1: Derrick Moore #8 and Jimmy Rolder #41 of the Detroit Lions celebrate after a sack during the third quarter against the Minnesota Vikings at Ford Field on November 1, 2026 in Detroit, Michigan. (Photo by Todd Rosenberg/Getty Images) | Getty Images

In Week 8, the Detroit Lions moved to 5-2 on the season and 2-0 in the NFC North after taking down the NFL’s last remaining undefeated team: the division rival Minnesota Vikings.

Let’s look at the snap counts from this game and see what they mean for the depth chart hierarchy and what we can ascertain moving forward.

Quarterback

Jared Goff: 72 (100%)

Josh Dobbs: DNP

If you just looked at the box score, you may think Goff was not his usual self, but he showed tremendous poise under consistent pressure—the Vikings blitzed nearly 90% of the time—and kept his head when it mattered.

Running back

Jahmyr Gibbs: 55 (76%)

Sione Vaki: 20 (28%) — 16 special teams snaps (70%)

Jacob Saylors: 0 (0%) — 7 (30%) — Injured (neck)

Whew, what a game. The Lions ran the ball 16 times for 66 yards in the first half, with Gibbs accounting for 37 yards on 11 carries (3.4 yards per carry), while Vaki had five runs for 29 yards (5.8 ypc). But the dedication to the run game, coupled with more inside trap plays, opened things up in the second half, as Gibbs took his 12 carries for 116 yards (9.7 ypc) and Vaki delivered 36 yards on six carries (6.0 ypc).

Gibbs will be all over the highlight reels this week—and deservedly so—but it’s important not to overlook the “huge step” Vaki took in this game and why he was able to earn “a lot of trust” with this coaching staff. Vaki consistently gained positive yardage on his runs, which allowed the Lions to scale back Gibbs’ workload and should give the Lions tremendous confidence moving forward that they have two legitimate options in the backfield.

Wide receiver

Jameson Williams: 60 (83%)

Amon-Ra St. Brown: 52 (72%)

Isaac TeSlaa: 26 (36%)

Tay Martin: 2 (3%) — 16 (70%)

DeAndre Carter: 0 (0%) — 8 (35%)

Despite playing the No. 1 defense in the NFL, it was rinse and repeat for the Lions receivers. Their offensive splits and contributions were close to their season average—TeSlaa’s was scaled back a bit due to the Lions’ two tight end sets—as St. Brown was the volume option, Williams was the deep threat (he has a 46-yard reception), and all three were smashing people in the run game. St. Brown’s arena football formation was technically considered a run because Goff threw the ball slightly backward, which gave the Lions another 10 yards to their rushing totals.

Kids across Michigan are about to be lining up like this on playgrounds across the state.

Amon-Ra St. Brown got a HUGE running start pic.twitter.com/yUUX9nwnra
— Brad Galli (@BradGalli) November 1, 2026

Tight end

Sam LaPorta: 67 (93%)

Brock Wright: 55 (76%) — 5 (22%)

Tyler Conklin: 22 (31%) — 1 (4%)

Jackson Meeks: DNP (INACTIVE)

The NFL has struggled with the Vikings’ “double mug” blitzing concepts for some time now, but Lions offensive coordinator Drew Petzing unlocked the puzzle by deploying two tight ends in the backfield—LaPorta and Wright—and running an inside trap blocking scheme. This unique wrinkle complicated the Vikings’ aggressive approach by countering with their own aggressive downhill blocking and shifting the “gaps” of the Lions’ front.

Lions used their TEs in the backfield very effectively today against the Vikings defense. Adding and changing gaps for the defense to account for to get to zone runs and change-ups off of that.

The sidecar look on the first few clips has seen an uptick in the NFL the past month pic.twitter.com/7iTkKJ7pLz
— Nate Tice (@Nate_Tice) November 1, 2026

With the Lions finding success in this approach and leaning into it in the second half, Wright saw his highest number of offensive snaps since Week 11 of last season. Additionally, according to The Athletic’s Colton Pouncy, the Lions saw a large uptick in 13 personnel (three tight end sets), utilizing the formation 16 times against the Vikings (previously they used it 19 times through the first seven weeks) and had a success rate of 73.7%.

Offensive line

LG Christian Mahogany: 72 (100%) — 4 (17%)

RG Tate Ratledge: 72 (100%) — 4 (17%)

RT Blake Miller: 72 (100%) — 4 (17%)

LT Penei Sewell: 72 (100%)

C Juice Scruggs: 50 (69%) — 4 (17%)

C Cade Mays: 22 (31%) — Injured (ankle)

LT/6th OL: Larry Borom: 1 (1%) — 4 (17%)

RG Miles Frazier: 0 (0%) — 4 (17%)

C Seth McLaughlin: DNP (INACTIVE)

The Lions offensive line had a strong game, showing flashes of dominance in the fourth quarter that should remind fans of the 2023 unit that bullied teams. While Sewell was flagged for four penalties, he was a monster in the rushing attack, and the Lions ran behind him all game. The guards continue to excel and improve, while Miller remains steady, which is all you can ask from a rookie against the Vikings’ confusing front.

Mays continued to shine since his return, but an early injury knocked him out of the game, and Scruggs stepped back into a starting center role. While the Lions’ run game took off after Scruggs entered the game, I believe that was more due to a second-half shift in blocking philosophy, but that shouldn’t discount Scruggs’ impact, as it’s an incredible luxury to have a player who can seamlessly step in and help the OL dominate.

Interior defensive line

3T Alim McNeill: 40 (75%) — 3 (13%)

3T Skyler Gill-Howard: 27 (51%) — 2 (9%)

DT Tyleik Williams: 25 (47%) — 2 (9%)

DL Levi Onwuzurike: 7 (13%)

3T Mekhi Wingo: DNP (INACTIVE)

While the rest of the defense has undergone some change in snap distributions, the interior defensive line has stayed pretty consistent. With the Lions deploying more pass rush, Gill-Howard gets a slight edge in snaps over Williams—and the rookie rewarded the team with a sack—but we could see these two flip snap counts in future weeks.

EDGE

EDGE Aidan Hutchinson: 50 (94%) — 1 (4%)

Rush End Derrick Moore: 22 (42%) — 3 (13%)

Big End Tyler Lacy: 20 (38%) — 4 (17%)

Rush End DJ Wonnum: 16 (30%) — 2 (9%) — Injured (concussion)

Rush End Eric O’Neill: 8 (15%) — 10 (43%)

Big End Ahmed Hassanein: DNP (INACTIVE)

After Wonnum was forced from the game with a concussion, the Lions leaned more on rookie Derrick Moore to fill in at the rush edge. While coaches tend to prefer to lean on their veterans in these situations, they didn’t deviate from their player roles and went to Moore, allowing Lacy to stay in the big-end-only role. For the second week in a row, O’Neill is getting sprinkled into obvious pass-rushing situations.

Linebacker

MIKE Jack Campbell: 41 (77%) — 2 (9%) — Injured (neck)

SAM Derrick Barnes: 28 (53%) — 6 (26%)

WILL/SAM Trevor Nowaske: 26 (49%) — 19 (83%)

MIKE Jimmy Rolder: 17 (32%) — 13 (57%) — Injured (hamstring)

WILL/MIKE Malcolm Rodriguez: 15 (28%) — 16 (70%)

WILL Amen Ogbongbemiga: 0 (0%) — 16 (70%)

The Lions entered this game with an apparent plan to rotate some of their linebacker roles, with the exception of Jack Campbell. Unfortunately, his scary neck injury forced him out, and with Rolder also exiting with a hamstring injury, the Lions had to shuffle their linebackers even more so.

Overall, the plan appeared to be to scale back Barnes, increase Nowaske, and get Rolder on the field for significant reps, but the injuries altered roles and opened the door for Rodriguez to expand his role. Watching live, it wasn’t clear who the primary MIKE linebacker was—the All-22 was not yet available at the time of publication—but it looked like both Barnes and Rodruguez stepped into different spots.

Ogbongbemiga was the only defensive player not to play on defense in this game.

Cornerback

CB D.J. Reed: 42 (79%) — Injured (hip)

CB/NB Roger McCreary: 41 (77%) — 3 (13%)

CB Rock Ya-Sin: 24 (45%) — 2 (9%)

CB Khalil Dorsey: 21 (40%) — 18 (78%)

CB Ennis Rakestraw: 1 (2%) — 5 (22%)

Reed was forced from the game with a hip injury, but he was made available in the locker room following the game, which is typically a good sign his injury won’t be a long-term one. Reed has been sensational of late, and in the last three weeks has leveled up his game:

The top-graded NFL cornerback in Weeks 5-8, according to PFF:

Lions CB D.J. Reed

He's got a 90.7 PFF grade with a 91.0 coverage grade (also 1st) over that span.
— Jeremy Reisman (@DetroitOnLion) November 2, 2026

McCreary saw his reps scaled back from previous weeks and continues to rep both inside and out, but it appeared he made room for Ya-Sin to see a large increase in snaps, his largest since being benched after Week 2. Dorsey continues to step up in “and-long” and third-down situations, while Rakestraw was limited to only one snap, which came after Reed was sidelined.

Safety

S Chuck Clark: 53 (100%) — 6 (26%)

DB Keith Abney: 28 (53%) — 6 (26%)

S Brian Branch: 23 (43%) — Injured (concussion)

DB Christian Izien: 8 (15%) — 12 (52%)

S Bishop Fitzgerald: DNP (INACTIVE)

With Branch exiting early with a concussion, Clark saw his playing time expand and opened the door up for Abney to get back in the mix. Izien was deployed in specific situations vs. the tight ends, but he continues to struggle with his assignments.

Specialists

K Jake Bates: 9 (39%)

P Jack Fox: 8 (35%)

LS Hogan Hatten: 8 (35%)

Bates missed his first kick of the season in this game, but the Lions were able to roll with it, and it didn’t become too much of a factor in the end.

michigan.headline: 2027 three-star OL Sidney Rouleau decommits from Michigan Football
michigan.body:
ANN ARBOR, MICHIGAN - SEPTEMBER 12: The offensive line (L-R) Jalen Hoffman #42, Andrew Sprague #54, Brady Norton #70, Jake Guarnera #53, Nathan Efobi #55, and Blake Frazier #77 of the Michigan Wolverines run to the line of scrimmage during the first half of a college football game against the Oklahoma Sooners at Michigan Stadium on September 12, 2026 in Ann Arbor, Michigan. The Michigan Wolverines won the game 17-10. (Photo by Aaron J. Thornton/Getty Images) | Getty Images

The Wolverines lost a piece to their 2027 recruiting class, as three-star offensive lineman Sidney Rouleau announced his decommitment from Michigan Football on Tuesday.

🚨BREAKING🚨 2027 IOL Sidney Rouleau has decommitted from Michigan, @SWiltfong_ reports.https://t.co/DAuehAHfht pic.twitter.com/kvNfT6drlI
— Rivals (@Rivals) November 3, 2026

The 6-foot-5, 265-pounder from Canada originally committed to the Wolverines back in March, but he took a visit to Syracuse during Halloween weekend for the Orange’s upset win over SMU. Syracuse has been making a “strong push to flip him,” according to Brice Marich of The Michigan Insider ($), so it wouldn’t be a surprise to see him wind up playing his college football in the ACC.

Additionally, Rivals’ Steve Wiltfong ($) reported earlier today that Michigan is “moving on” from Rouleau. This makes sense, considering offensive line coach Jim Harding has offered other interior offensive linemen this fall. Two of them — former NC State commit Conner Rutherford and current Stanford commit and in-state prospect Braden Chaffin — are actually set to visit Ann Arbor this weekend for the rivalry matchup against MSU.

But losing a longtime member of your recruiting class is never something to be happy about, no matter if they wanted to go somewhere else or if the program itself decided to not honor his commitment anymore. Rouleau was offered by the coaching staff for a reason, so it’s interesting the Wolverines are moving on from him so close to the beginning of the early signing period. Whatever the exact reasons may be, we certainly wish him all the best wherever he ends up at.

The Wolverines now have three offensive linemen — Jakari Lipsey, Lincoln Mageo and Louis Esposito — and 21 total committed prospects in their 2027 class.

michigan.headline: Wolverines in the NFL: Blake Corum scores again, Josh Metellus makes 13 tackles
michigan.body:
INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA - NOVEMBER 1: Blake Corum #24 of the Los Angeles Rams carries the ball during the third quarter of an NFL football game against the Los Angeles Chargers at SoFi Stadium on November 1, 2026 in Inglewood, California. (Photo by Brooke Sutton/Getty Images) | Getty Images

Blake Corum scored for the second straight week, and two other former Michigan Wolverines helped the Rams keep the Chargers out of the end zone. Six Michigan alumni took the field at Ford Field as the Lions handed the Vikings their first loss of the season. And on Monday night, two former Michigan tight ends faced off in Seattle.

Here’s how the Wolverines fared in Week 8 of the 2026 NFL season.

Blake Corum gets the Rams’ ground game going

The Rams had just 10 rushing yards at halftime against the Chargers. Corum more than doubled that on one play in the third quarter, breaking free for a 23-yard touchdown that turned a one-point lead into a 17-9 advantage. He finished with a team-high 73 yards on 11 carries, averaging 6.6 yards per attempt in the 24-9 win.

Blake Corum with the smooth move and TD!

LACvsLAR on FOX/FOX One
Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/YP3lqMMQYg
— NFL (@NFL) November 1, 2026

The Rams had two more former Wolverines making plays on defense. Edge rusher Josaiah Stewart finished with six tackles and a sack, while cornerback Josh Wallace made four tackles, including three solo stops.

Josh Metellus makes 13 tackles as Detroit hands Minnesota its first loss

Metellus finished with 13 tackles and a pass breakup in Minnesota’s 19-15 loss at Ford Field. On the other side, Aidan Hutchinson made four solo tackles and forced a fumble. He played 50 of Detroit’s 53 defensive snaps, as the Lions held Minnesota to 266 total yards.

Rookies Derrick Moore and Jimmy Rolder also saw time on defense and special teams. Moore played 22 defensive snaps, and Rolder played 17 on defense and another 13 on special teams. Unfortunately, Rolder will miss the rest of the season due to a hamstring injury he suffered in this game.

For Minnesota, fullback Max Bredeson played seven offensive snaps, and guard Trevor Keegan appeared off the bench.

Colston Loveland leads Chicago in catches on Monday night

Loveland caught 7-of-9 targets for 65 yards against Seattle on Monday Night Football. He led the Bears in receptions and finished second in receiving yards.

On the other sideline, Seattle tight end AJ Barner turned his lone catch into a 17-yard gain on three targets. Former Michigan linebacker Devin Bush also saw action for Chicago.

DJ Turner II recovers two fumbles in Bengals’ overtime win

Turner recovered two fumbles and made three tackles as Cincinnati beat Tennessee, 43-36, in overtime. Unfortunately, Turner left the game in the fourth quarter due to injury, so hopefully he isn’t out for long.

Insane play from DJ Turner to force a fumble on this screen pic.twitter.com/8qTOQE6VJt
— mike (@bengals_sans) November 2, 2026

Fellow Bengals cornerback Daxton Hill made four solo tackles, defensive tackle Kris Jenkins added one, and William Wagner handled long-snapping duties.
